symptom: `move entity MyFirstModule.Item to Probe; alter entity Probe.Item set documentation 'text';` — check: "statement 2: entity not found: Probe.Item (referenced by alter entity)", exec: "Refusing to execute: … Nothing was written."; `--no-check` applies it and mx check is clean. Same for `rename entity M.Item to Thing; alter entity M.Thing …` ("— M has Item"). mendixlabs/mxcli#1601.
cause: validateAlterTarget's entity case accepted only sc.entities (what a CREATE declares). collectSingle already put MOVE/RENAME destinations in sc.indirectEntities, and the association-endpoint, grant, view-source and datagrid checks read it; the ALTER target check did not.
fix: Accept sc.indirectEntities[qn] alongside sc.entities[qn]. Test: TestValidateAlterTarget_CountsEntitiesAMoveOrRenameProduces (+ a control that a typo next to a move is still reported); bug test mdl-examples/bug-tests/1601-alter-entity-after-move-or-rename.mdl.
insight: The reporter's suggested site (the refs.entities loop in validate.go) was wrong: the message came from validateAlterTarget, which formats "(referenced by alter <kind>)" itself — grep the message's suffix, not its prefix. When a scriptContext set exists (indirectEntities), grep its readers: every consumer of sc.entities that skips it is a candidate for the same false 'not found'. A bug-test MDL must move INTO a module the project already has — checkAlterTarget skips script-created modules, so a fully self-contained script (create module Probe; move …) never reproduced it on the unfixed binary.
